bib.title: Automated flower classification over a large number of classes
bib.venue: Sixth Indian Conference on Computer Vision, Graphics & Image Processing (ICVGIP 2008), inferred from DOI 10.1109/icvgip.2008.47; the PDF text prints no venue

question: Can combining several hand-designed features in a learned multiple-kernel SVM improve classification over a large number of visually similar classes (flowers)?
hypothesis: Learning per-class optimum kernel combinations of colour, shape and texture features beats any single feature.
contributions: Four flower-specific features (internal SIFT, boundary SIFT, HOG, HSV colour) combined with per-class kernel weights (Varma and Ray)
Best result to date on the 17 class flower dataset (88.33%)

method.summary: Flowers are segmented (iterative graph-cut plus petal shape model), four bag-of-visual-words histograms are computed, and a one-vs-rest SVM with a weighted sum of chi-squared exponential kernels is trained, with per-class weights learnt by Varma and Ray's convex method.

datasets.name: 103 class flower dataset (later the Oxford Flowers dataset)
datasets.size: 8189 images, 103 classes, 40 to 250 images per class
datasets.split: train 10 per class (1030), validation 10 per class (1030), test remaining 6129 (min 20 per class)
datasets.source: mostly web images, a few taken by the authors; flowers common in the UK; images rescaled so smallest dimension is 500 pixels

datasets.name: 17 class flower dataset
datasets.source: Nilsback and Zisserman 2006, public at robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/data/flowers

models.name: Multiple-kernel SVM, 4 features
models.architecture: one-vs-rest SVM, K=sum_f beta_f exp(-mu_f chi2_f), mu_f = 1/mean chi2 distance over training images
models.vocab: visual words: 1000 colour, 8000 internal SIFT, 3000 boundary SIFT, 1500 HOG

training.objective: one-vs-rest SVM with learnt per-class kernel weights beta_f
training.optimizer: Varma and Ray 2007 convex optimization for beta_f

other.hyperparameter_search: vocabulary size 1000-10000 (colour 100-5000), SIFT radius and spacing 5-50 pixels, each tuned separately on validation set; then retrained on train+val

inference.decoding: class with most positive classifier response

metrics.name: recognition rate
metrics.definition: classification accuracy averaged over classes, not images

baselines: Varma and Ray 2007 MKL on same features
eval.protocol: Test on 6129 held-out images; 17-class results reported as mean +/- std (number of splits not stated)

evidence.quote: The training set and validation set each consist of 10 images per class (totalling 1030 images each). The test set consist of the remaining 6129 images (minimum 20 per class).

results.claim: All four features combined reach the best test recognition rate on the 103 class dataset.

limits: Paper states 103 classes throughout; the later widely used Oxford 102 Flowers dataset is a different release, not described here (102 appears nowhere in this text).
Number of 17-class splits/trials behind the +/- values is not stated.
No hardware, SVM C value or code given.
Hand-designed features and a small training set (10 images per class); era-specific, long since surpassed by deep features.
Authors concede large within-class variation and few samples are the principal challenge.
